Unexpectedly, this even happens when the curve is perfectly straight:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47f867ca-242b-4bde-ad79-9cc68a11feaf)

I suppose you can use `tessellate_even_length()`.

Looking at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/62301, it seems that `bake_interval` is used like a limit value for calculating the optimal point. However, indeed, the property name is misleading and the documentation may need to be updated (and perhaps the property names should be renamed in Godot 5.0).

Hello @TokageItLab,

I also tried to use `tesselate_even_length()`, but it behaves pretty much the same as the baked_points:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea669198-77a2-4a27-a3df-f02ae34c9ee0)

Code:
```gdscript
@tool
extends Node2D

@export var bake_interval := 5.0:
	set(value):
		bake_interval = value
		queue_redraw()

@export var force_update := false:
	set(value):
		queue_redraw()

func _draw():
	var baked_curve: Curve2D = $BakedPath.curve
	baked_curve.bake_interval = bake_interval
	var baked_points = baked_curve.get_baked_points()

	for point in baked_points:
		draw_set_transform(point, 0.0, Vector2.ONE)
		draw_circle(Vector2.ZERO, 2, Color.RED)

	var tesselated_curve: Curve2D = $TesselateEvenPath.curve
	var tesselated_points = tesselated_curve.tessellate_even_length()

	for point in tesselated_points:
		draw_set_transform(point, 0.0, Vector2.ONE)
		draw_circle(Vector2.ZERO, 2, Color.MAGENTA)
```

For 2D this is caused by #69115, happens since v4.0.beta8.official [45cac42c0]. Same issue for 3D. > I also tried to use `tesselate_even_length()`, but it behaves pretty much the same as the baked_points Indeed both are using the same function internally. The difference is that the default baking uses `p_max_stages = 10` and `p_length = bake_interval`, while the exposed `tesselate_even_length` method uses `max_stages = 5` and `p_length = 20.0` by default (so it doesn't use `bake_interval` unless manually passed to it). `curve.tessellate_even_length(10, curve.bake_interval)` would be equivalent to `curve.get_baked_points()`.
Relevant source (click to expand)

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L909-L937 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/scene/resources/curve.h#L253 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L1312-L1315

--- The main issue / cause of the behavior is that the subdivision steps are done by using `real_t mp = (p_begin + p_end) * 0.5;` for the subsequent bezier interpolation-sampling, but the distance along the curve is not linear to such parameter, hence taking the middle value doesn't mean the 2 sub-curves have the same length. And thus the final point density is affected. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L866-L880 Example visualization for a simple straight line curves: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1b0b127-ac94-41bd-9fe4-9049e042ff4d)|![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df1a2eae-4dd1-4cb5-8005-8a4f0686dda2) -|- ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e79911cf-1816-4c3f-824b-26fc6ab32280)|![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b797cc10-f19c-47fe-b8e7-54c5936a211e) Not sure if it's bad / needs changing. For sure the docs of `bake_interval` are misleading / needs fixing. --- Here's a potential workaround / how you could obtain actually evenly spaced points: ```gdscript assert(curve.point_count > 0) var interval: float = curve.bake_interval var length: float = curve.get_baked_length() var point_count: int = 1 + floori(length / interval) var evenly_spaced_points: PackedVector2Array evenly_spaced_points.resize(point_count) for i: int in point_count: evenly_spaced_points[i] = curve.sample_baked(i * interval) ``` --- > Godot v4.4.1-stable: `MEAN: 0.19463709623233, STD_DEV: 0.0088449005702, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 1025` > > ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5794ba62-5054-4fb9-8338-7706f81ced76) > > Is there any reason why the mean distance between baked points is not correct in the case of Godot v4.4.1-stable? Regarding this, the data shows that the distances are bigger than the `bake_interval`, which means that the default subdivision steps limit was reached. And indeed the point count is 1025 which is `2^10 + 1` where `10` is the default steps limit. Doing `curve.tessellate_even_length(max_steps, curve.bake_interval)` with `max_steps > 10` should give results with better mean / standard deviation (and more points). And indeed for the curve from the MRP: ``` MAX_STEPS: 10, MEAN: 0.19463709623233, STD_DEV: 0.0088449005702, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 1025 MAX_STEPS: 11, MEAN: 0.09731855149403, STD_DEV: 0.00221122744972, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 2049 MAX_STEPS: 12, MEAN: 0.07057662664388, STD_DEV: 0.00025114867027, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 2825 MAX_STEPS: 13, MEAN: 0.06765390141853, STD_DEV: 0.00022000642563, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 2947 MAX_STEPS: 14, MEAN: 0.06765390141853, STD_DEV: 0.00022000642563, SIZE OF BAKED POINTS: 2947 ``` As already mentioned, the `bake_interval` is currently being used as subdivision limiter, not as the target distance between the baked points, and that's why the final mean distance is way smaller than the `bake_interval`.

I have the same issue @2shady4u describes here: I'm trying to create player controlled movement for a snake-like character and after a few weeks of iteration testing various approaches I finally came to conclusion Curves is the only way to go in my usecase. Now I'm completely stumped.
Did you test the workarounds? Are they no longer working?

The workaround does not use any of the problematic properties or methods, so why would it not work? Also, if you want to know if a workaround works, please just copy and paste it and try yourself. It would have taken you the same amount of time you spend writing your comment.

These properties and methods clearly don't do what they are supposed to do, or if they do they then have a false name and description and this class is lacking an important feature.

You were asking for ways to work with this type, the workarounds are the way to do that until a fix is available, I asked because it seemed like you were saying you were unable to make things work for your project, hence the confusion, if the workarounds work then that's what you need to use until some improvement can be made (you are very welcome to help with that as well)
